extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO counsel, and attorneys/agents facing or advising on USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order resolving USPTO disciplinary action by stipulation; sets out jurisdiction, definitions (e.g., conviction, serious crime), rule violated, respondent's duties, and the agreed sanctions and publication/administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this proceeding pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against registered practitioners are brought under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions; disciplinary agreements and final orders are processed and approved under these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: At all relevant times, Respondent was registered to practice before the USPTO in patent matters and subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration information (registration number, date of registration, state bar licensure) is relevant to establishing that the practitioner is governed by the USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of conviction (37 C.F.R. § 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A guilty plea is a conviction pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1, which defines conviction to include 'any confession to a crime; a verdict or judgment finding a person guilty of a crime; any entered plea, including nolo contender or Alford plea, to a crime; or receipt of deferred adjudication...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entered guilty plea (or other listed forms) may constitute a conviction for USPTO disciplinary purposes even where sentence or judgment status varies; such convictions can form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of serious crime (37 C.F.R. § 11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conspiracy to Commit Health Care Fraud is a serious crime pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1, where 'serious crime' is defined as (1) any criminal offense classified as a felony, or (2) any crime a serious element of which includes interference with administration of justice, false swearing, misrepresentation, fraud, willful failure to file income tax returns, deceit, bribery, extortion, misappropriation, theft, or an attempt/conspiracy/solicitation to commit such a crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crimes classified as felonies or those containing enumerated elements are treated as 'serious crimes' for disciplinary analysis; the presence of such crimes supports more severe disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) (criminal conduct reflecting adversely on fitness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's acts and omissions violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b): committing a criminal act that reflects adversely on his honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner, or being convicted of a crime that so reflects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A conviction for a serious crime or committing criminal conduct that calls into question honesty/trustworthiness/fitness supports a finding of professional misconduct under § 11.804(b) and forms a basis for sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties upon interim suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent complied with his duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 in connection with the February 17, 2022 Final Order of interim suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners subject to interim suspension must follow the notification, client-matter-handling, and other duties specified in § 11.58; compliance may affect timing or characterization of subsequent discipline (e.g., deemed commencement date of suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice (term and commencement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office for a period of five (5) years; in light of compliance with duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, the five-year suspension is deemed to have commenced on February 17, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions (here, suspension and its duration) are specified in the Final Order; compliance with interim-suspension duties can cause the formal sanction to be deemed to have commenced earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on USPTO electronic accounts during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO verified Electronic System account, obtain such an account, nor have his name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account or a USPTO.gov account, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners are barred from accessing or being added to USPTO electronic systems until reinstatement; this is an explicit operational restriction tied to the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Order does not preclude future discipline for unrelated misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall be construed as preventing the USPTO from seeking future discipline for violations for misconduct unrelated to the conviction addressed in this Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement of one matter does not immunize the practitioner from later proceedings based on separate misconduct; the Office retains authority to pursue other complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings or reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of similar misconduct concerning Respondent; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline, and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf; and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records may be used as aggravating evidence, to rebut representations, or in reconsideration requests; respondents should understand that settlements/orders become part of their disciplinary history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED's FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' text describing the conviction, rule violated, and sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions are publicly disclosed via OED reading room and Official Gazette; the Final Order includes standardized notice language to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to seek reconsideration or review
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on Respondent's agreement, Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may include express waivers of procedural rights to seek reconsideration, review, or appeal; agreeing to such waivers finalizes the disciplinary resolution subject to the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-order procedural step: dismissal without prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a reasonable period after entry of the Final Order approving this Agreement, the OED Director shall file a motion dismissing the pending disciplinary action without prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal pending disciplinary case may be dismissed following entry of a settlement-based Final Order; dismissal without prejudice preserves the Office's ability to initiate future proceedings on other grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may provide that each party bears its own costs rather than awarding costs to either side.
